parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic آب (ʔāb), from Classical Syriac ܐܒ.
Borrowed from Arabic آدَم (ʔādam), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew אָדָם (āḏā́m), from Proto-Semitic *ʔadam-.
Borrowed from Arabic آدَمِيّ (ʔādamiyy). By surface analysis, آدم (ādam /âdam) + ـی (-ī /-i, noun forming suffix).
Borrowed from Arabic آدَمِيَّة (ʔādamiyya, “humanity”). By surface analysis, آدم (âdam, “human”) + ـیت (-iyyat, “-ity”).
Borrowed from Arabic آذَار (ʔāḏār), from Classical Syriac ܐܕܪ.
Borrowed from Arabic آمِينَ (ʔāmīna), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܰܡܺܝܢ (ʾāmēn) or Aramaic אַמִין (ʾāmēn).
Borrowed from Arabic آيَةُ اللّٰه (ʔāyatu llāh).

parole.significato: verse (of a holy book, such as the Qur'an or Bible)
ʾabābīl, the flock of birds that destroyed the army of Abraha in the Year of the Elephant (often said to be swallows)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَبَابِيل (ʔabābīl), a Quranic hapax legomena.
Borrowed from Arabic إِبَاضِيّ (ʔibāḍiyy). By surface analysis, اباض (ebâz) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: Ibadism, the doctrines associated with Ibadis, such as the acceptance of fewer hadiths, and the addition of Jami Sahih…

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَبْجَد (ʔabjad), equivalent to the first four letters of the Perso-Arabic script in the traditional order: ا (vowel placeholder), ب (b), ج (j), د (d).
Borrowed from Arabic إِبْرِيق (ʔibrīq), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܒܪܝܩܐ (ʾaḇrēqā), possibly borrowed from Middle Persian *ābrēk, or possibly borrowed from Parthian *ābrēk.

parole.significato: maintaining, retaining (e.g. a position of power)
ibn; a word meaning "son", used only in patronymic names and certain literary expressions borrowed from Arabic.
only used in kunyas (teknonyms) borrowed from Arabic and kunya-like Arabic loanwords or pseudo-Arabisms
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَبُو (ʔabū), nominative construct state of أَب (ʔab, “father”).
Borrowed from Arabic أَبُو الْهَوْل (ʔabū l-hawl). By surface analysis, ابو (abū /abu) + الـ (al-) + هول (hawl /howl).
Borrowed from Arabic اِتِّحَاد (ittiḥād), from اِتَّحَدَ (ittaḥada).

parole.significato: union (something formed by a combination or coalition of parts or members)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic اِتِّفَاق (ittifāq). Sense 5 in Dari is a semantic borrowing from Indo-Persian.
Borrowed from Arabic اِجْتِمَاع (ijtimāʕ), from اِجْتَمَعَ (ijtamaʕa).
Borrowed from Arabic اِجْتِمَاعِيّ (ijtimāʕiyy). By surface analysis, اجتماع (ejtemâ', “society, community”) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic إِحَاطَة (ʔiḥāṭa), from أَحَاطَ (ʔaḥāṭa).
Borrowed from Arabic اِحْتِيَاط (iḥtiyāṭ), from اِحْتَاطَ (iḥtāṭa).
Borrowed from Arabic أَحْسَنْتَ (ʔaḥsanta, masculine) / أَحْسَنْتِ (ʔaḥsanti, feminine), meaning "you have done well."
Borrowed from Arabic اِخْتِيَارِيّ (iḵtiyāriyy). By surface analysis, اختیار (extiyâr, “choice”) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic أَخْلَاقِيّ (ʔaḵlāqiyy). By surface analysis, اخلاق (axlâq) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: recent; the most recent; latest; last (in time, chronological order)
office (a building or room where clerical or professional duties are performed)
politeness, courtesy, civility, manners, proper conduct

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَدَبِيَّات (ʔadabiyyāt). By surface analysis, ادب (adab) + ـیات (-iyyât).
Borrowed from Arabic أَذَان (ʔaḏān, “call to prayer”).
Borrowed from Arabic إِرَادَة (ʔirāda), from أَرَادَ (ʔarāda).
Borrowed from Arabic أَرْبَاب (ʔarbāb), originally the plural of رَبّ (rabb, “lord”).
Borrowed from Arabic اِرْتِجَاعِيّ (irtijāʕiyy). By surface analysis, ارتجاع (ertejâ') + ـی (-i).
Borrowed from Arabic اِرْتِقَاء (irtiqāʔ), from اِرْتَقَى (irtaqā).

parole.significato: inheritance (that which is entitled to inherit)
anaphora (An expression that can refer to virtually any referent)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَرْض (ʔarḍ), from Proto-Semitic *ʔarṣ́-.

parole.significato: exchange; used in به ازای (be ezâ-ye, “in exchange for”) and در ازای (dar ezâ-ye, “in exchange for”).
pre-eternity, eternity without beginning; the era before God created space and time
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَزَل (ʔazal), from Middle Persian 𐭫𐭠𐭮 (ʾsl /⁠asar⁠/, “endless”), from 𐭠 (ʾ- /⁠a-⁠/, “un-, without”) + 𐭫𐭮 (sl /⁠sar⁠/, “head; beginning; end”, whence modern سر (sar)).
From Arabic ء س ر (ʔ s r).
Borrowed from Arabic أَسَاسًا (ʔasāsan). By surface analysis, اساس (asâs) + ـا (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic اِسْتِثْنَائِيّ (istiṯnāʔiyy). By surface analysis, استثنا (estesnâ) + ـیی (-yi).

parole.significato: act like a donkey; act stupidly or naively.
fortification (especially one that fully encircles the defended position)
parole.testo: Arabic plural of استحکام (estehkâm), from Arabic اِسْتِحْكَام (istiḥkām, “intensification, becoming fortified”). Probably a calque of French fortification, likely via Ottoman Turkish استحكامات (istihkamat).
Borrowed from Arabic أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّٰه (ʔastaḡfiru llāh).

parole.significato: disregard for the help of others; independence, ability to be independent
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic اِسْتِغْنَاء (istiḡnāʔ), verbal noun of اِسْتَغْنَى (istaḡnā, “to be rich; to do without”).

parole.significato: A rhetorical question in which the speaker means to say the answer is negative.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic اِسْتِفْهَام إِنْكَارِيّ (istifhām ʔinkāriyy).

parole.significato: welcoming, reception, going out to meet
relying on, drawing upon (e.g. a source)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أُسْطُوَانَة (ʔusṭuwāna), from Aramaic אִיסְטְוָונָא (ʾesṭwānā, “column, pillar”), from Middle Persian stwn' (stūn, “column, pillar”). Compare ستون (sotun, “pillar, column”).

parole.significato: astrolabe, an astronomical and navigational instrument for gauging the altitude of the Sun and stars
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَسْطُرْلَاب (ʔasṭurlāb), which derives from Ancient Greek ἀστρολάβος (astrolábos).
Borrowed from Arabic أُسْطُورَة (ʔusṭūra, “fable, myth”), from Ancient Greek ἱστορία (historía, “inquiry, examination”).
Borrowed from Arabic إِسْفَنْج (ʔisfanj), borrowed from Ancient Greek σπόγγος (spóngos).

parole.significato: bishop, an official governing a diocese
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أُسْقُف (ʔusquf), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܦܣܩܘܦܐ (ʾeppisqoppā), borrowed from Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos), from ἐπι- (epi-, “upon”) + σκοπός (skopós, “watcher, lookout, guardian”).

parole.significato: method, manner, mode, style, technique, way

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِشَارَة (ʔišāra), from أَشَارَ (ʔašāra).
Borrowed from Arabic اِشْتِرَاك (ištirāk), from اِشْتَرَكَ (ištaraka).

parole.significato: appetite (desire of or relish for food)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَشْخَاص (ʔašḵāṣ), plural of Arabic شَخْص (šaḵṣ).

parole.significato: A horse (or some other mammal) with only one testicle.
parole.testo: From Arabic أَشْرَج (ʔašraj), with the same meaning.
Borrowed from Arabic إِشْفَاق (ʔišfāq), verbal noun of أَشْفَقَ (ʔašfaqa), sometimes also understood as أَشْفَاق (ʔašfāq), the plural of شَفَق (šafaq).
Borrowed from Arabic أَصَالَة (ʔaṣāla, “being rooted; being established”).
Borrowed from Arabic إِصْطَبْل (ʔiṣṭabl), via Byzantine Greek στάβλον (stáblon) from Latin stabulum.
Borrowed from Arabic أَصْلِيّ (ʔaṣliyy), from أَصْل (ʔaṣl) + ـِيّ (-iyy).
Borrowed from Arabic إِضَافَة (ʔiḍāfa), from أَضَافَ (ʔaḍāfa).
Borrowed from Arabic اِطِّلَاع (iṭṭilāʕ), from اِطَّلَعَ (iṭṭalaʕa).
Borrowed from Arabic أَطْلَس, from Ancient Greek Ἄτλας (Átlas).
Borrowed from Arabic اِعْتِبَار (iʕtibār), from اِعْتَبَرَ (iʕtabara).
Borrowed from Arabic اِعْتِرَاض (iʕtirāḍ), from اِعْتَرَضَ (iʕtaraḍa).

parole.significato: i'tikaf (the retreat into a mosque for worship, especially during the last 10 days of Ramadan or the Night of Power)

parole.testo: Pseudo-Arabism from the root ع ز م (ʕ z m).

Borrowed from Arabic أَعْشَارِيّة (ʔaʕšāriyya), the feminine of أَعْشَارِيّ (ʔaʕšāriyy, “decimal”), a term from the plural of عُشْر (ʕušr, “tenth”) that did not catch on after having been employed in the 19th century.
Borrowed from Arabic إِعْلَامِيَّة (ʔiʕlāmiyya), from إِعْلَامِيّ (ʔiʕlāmiyy) or ـَة (-a).
Pseudo-Arabism from Arabic اِغْتِشَاش (iḡtišāš) verbal noun of اِغْتَشَّ (iḡtašša, “to be deceived, to be adulterated”) (form VIII).
Borrowed from Arabic اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة (iftitāḥiyya). By surface analysis, افتتاح (iftitāh /eftetâh) + ـیه (-iyya /-iye).
Borrowed from Arabic اِفْتِخَار (iftiḵār, “haughtiness, loftiness”). Compare Arabic فَخْر (faḵr, “honour, pride”).

parole.significato: more or most excellent, virtuous, distinguished, eminent, learned, noble
iftar (the evening meal that breaks each day's fast during Ramadan, traditionally beginning with dates and water)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَفْلَاطُونِيّ (ʔaflāṭūniyy). By surface analysis, افلاطون (aflâtun) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Derived from Arabic إِقَامَة (ʔiqāma). Doublet of اقامه (eqâme, “iqama”).

parole.significato: iqama (the second call to prayer, made immediately before Muslims pray)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِقَامَة (ʔiqāma). Doublet of اقامت (“residence”).

parole.significato: adaptation (of a literary work, a work of fiction)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic اِقِتِصَادِيّ (iqitiṣādiyy). By surface analysis, اقتصاد (eqtesâd) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic إِقْلِيم (ʔiqlīm), from Ancient Greek κλίμα (klíma).

Borrowed from Arabic أُوقْيَانُوس (ʔūqyānūs), from Ancient Greek ὠκεανός (ōkeanós). First attested in the Iqbāl-nāma, circa 1195, but as a foreign یونانی (yūnānī /yunâni, “Ancient Greek”) word for "deep sea," and uncommon until the 1800s. The widespread modern use is influenced by European languages
Borrowed from Arabic الْآنَ (al-ʔāna), from آن (ʔān, “time”).

parole.significato: praise be to God, thank God, alhamdulillah; a common expression of gratitude, relief, or joy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ (al-ḥamdu lillāhi).
From Arabic إِلَخ (ʔilaḵ), an abbreviation of إِلَىٰ آخِرِهِ (ʔilā ʔāḵirihi).
Borrowed from Arabic إِلْزَامَات (ʔilzāmāt), plural of إِلْزَام (ʔilzām).
Borrowed from Arabic إِلْزَامِيّ (ʔilzāmiyy). By surface analysis, الزام (elzâm, “requirement”) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: Used in certain unadapted borrowings from Arabic.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic ال (al-, “the”, definite article).

parole.significato: alif (the letter ا, the first letter of the Persian and Arabic abjads)

parole.testo: From Arabic أَلِفْبَاء (ʔalifbāʔ), named after the first two letters of the Arabic alphabet.
Arabic إِلٰهِيَّات (ʔilāhiyyāt, “theology, lit. "divine things"”), from إِلٰهِيّ (ʔilāhiyy, “divine”).
From Arabic الْيَوْم (al-yawm). By surface analysis, الـ (al-) + یوم (yawm /yowm)
Borrowed from Arabic إِمَارَة (ʔimāra), from أَمَرَ (ʔamara).
Borrowed from Arabic إِمَامة (ʔimāma), from إِمَام (ʔimām) + ـَة (-a).
Borrowed from Arabic أَمَانَة (ʔamāna), from أَمُنَ (ʔamuna).
Borrowed from Arabic إِمْلَاء (ʔimlāʔ), from أَمْلَى (ʔamlā).
From Arabic أَمْلَاك (ʔamlāk), plural of مِلْك (milk).

parole.significato: secure; safe, especially against attacks, crime, etc.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَمْن (ʔamn, “security, safety”, noun).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إنَّا لِلّٰهِ وَإنَّا إلَيْهِ راجِعُون (ʔinnā lillāhi waʔinnā ʔilayhi rājiʕūn).

parole.significato: alembic (an early chemical apparatus, consisting of two retorts connected by a tube, used to purify substances by disti…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِنْبِيق (ʔinbīq), borrowed from Ancient Greek ἄμβιξ (ámbix).
Borrowed from Arabic اِنْتِخَابَات (intiḵābāt), plural of Arabic اِنْتِخَاب (intiḵāb).
Borrowed from Arabic اِنْتِظَار (intiẓār), from اِنْتَظَرَ (intaẓara).
Borrowed from Arabic اِنْتِهَاء (intihāʔ). See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

parole.significato: sociability, being acquaintanced, being familiar with others

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِنْسَان (ʔinsān), from Proto-Semitic *ʔināš- (“man, person”).
Borrowed from Arabic إِنْسَانِيّ (ʔinsāniyy). By surface analysis, انسان (insān /ensân) + ـی (-ī /-i, adjectival suffix).

parole.significato: humanity, civility, humaneness (quality of being a good human)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِنْسَانِيَّة (ʔinsāniyya). By surface analysis, انسان (insān /ensân) + ـیت (-iyyat).
Borrowed from Arabic إِنْعَام (ʔinʕām), from أَنْعَمَ (ʔanʕama).
Borrowed from Arabic اِنْفِرَادِيّ (infirādiyy⁩). By surface analysis, انفراد (enferâd) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic إِنْكَار (ʔinkār), from أَنْكَرَ (ʔankara).

parole.significato: inshallah, if God wills, God willing; hopefully, fingers crossed
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic إِنْ شَاءَ ٱللَّٰهُ (ʔin šāʔa llāhu).
Borrowed from Arabic أَهَالِي (ʔahālī), the informal pronunciation of أَهَالٍ (ʔahālin), plural of أَهْل (ʔahl).

parole.significato: inhabitant; native; citizen; often used as an equivalent of English "to be from"

parole.testo: Ezafe of اهل + خبره, from Arabic أَهْلُ الْخِبْرَةِ (ʔahlu l-ḵibrati, “people of experience”).
Ezafe of اهل + صنعت, from Arabic أَهْلُ الْصَّنْعَةِ (ʔahlu l-ṣṣanʕati, “people of the craft”).
Reborrowed from Arabic أَوَان (ʔawān), from Middle Persian ʾwʾm, ʾʾwʾm (āwām, “time, space of time; age, epoch; point of time, occasion”).
Borrowed from Arabic أَوْبَاش (ʔawbāš), plural of وَبَش (wabaš).

From Arabic أَوْج (ʔawj), from Persian اوگ (owg), from Middle Iranian, ultimately Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewg- (“related to increasement”). Cognate with Gilaki اوچوک (učuk, “soar”) and Sanskrit उच्च (ucca).

parole.significato: firstly, first of all (mainly in sequences and enumerations)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَوَّلًا (ʔawwalan), from the adverbial accusative of أَوَّل (ʔawwal). By surface analysis, اول (avval) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic أَوْلَاد (ʔawlād), plural of وَلَد (walad, “child”).
Borrowed from Arabic أَوْلَوِيَّة (ʔawlawiyya), from أَوْلَى (ʔawlā).
Borrowed from Arabic أَوْلَى (ʔawlā), elative of وَلِيّ (waliyy).
Borrowed from Arabic إِكْمَال (ʔikmāl), verbal noun of أَكْمَلَ (ʔakmala).
Borrowed from Arabic أَيَّار (ʔayyār), from Classical Syriac ܐܝܪ.
Borrowed from Arabic أَيْلُول (ʔaylūl), from Classical Syriac ܐܝܠܘܠ.
Borrowed from Arabic إِيمَان (ʔīmān), from آمَنَ (ʔāmana).

parole.significato: safe; secure, especially against hazards, accidents
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic آمِن (ʔāmin), with an imāla i-mutation. Compare Classical Persian لیکِنْ (lēkin) and بَلی (balē), from Arabic لٰكِنْ (lākin) and بَلَى (balā). Compare Kurdish hêmin.
Borrowed from Arabic أَيُّوبِيّ (ʔayyūbiyy). By surface analysis, ایوب (ayyub) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
From باری (bâri), a borrowing from Arabic بَارِئ (bāriʔ).
Borrowed from Arabic بَاعِث (bāʕiṯ, “raiser, one who raises”).
From Arabic بَاقِلّاء (bāqillāʔ, “broad bean (Vicia faba)”), from Aramaic בקילא (“broad bean (Vicia faba)”).
Borrowed from Arabic بَاقٍ (bāqin⁩), from the root ب ق ي (b q y).
Borrowed from Arabic بَامِيَة (bāmiya), of unknown origin; See there for more.
From Arabic بِدُونِ (bi-dūni), from the preposition بِ (bi-, “with”) + the preposition دُونَ (dūna, “without”).
Borrowed from Arabic بُرْج (burj), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܒܘܪܓܐ, borrowed from Latin burgus or Ancient Greek πύργος (púrgos). Doublet of برز (burz /borz).
Borrowed from Arabic بَرْزَخ (barzaḵ), from Parthian *bwrz-ʾxw (/⁠burz-axw⁠/), from Parthian bwrz (/⁠burz⁠/, “high”) + ʾxw (/⁠axw⁠/, “world”).
From Arabic بلهوت (balahut, “A volcano in Yemen”).

parole.significato: bismillah, in the name of God
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic بِسْمِ ٱللّٰه (bismi llāh)
Borrowed from Arabic بَعْثِيّ (baʕṯiyy). By surface analysis, بعث (ba's, “Baath”) + ـی (-ī /-i, adjectival suffix).
Borrowed from Arabic بَعْضًا (baʕḍan). By surface analysis, بعض (ba'z) + ـا (-an).
Pseudo-Arabism, derived from Arabic بِلَا (bilā, “without”) + Persian تَکْلِیف (taklīf /taklif).
Borrowed from Arabic بِلَا صَاحِب (bilā ṣāḥib). By surface analysis, بلا (belâ, “without”) + صاحب (sâheb, “owner”).
Borrowed from Arabic بَلَى (balā). For the vowel change in Classical Persian compare لیکِن (lēkin), from Arabic لَٰكِن (lākin).

parole.significato: only used in بناءً علی هٰذا (benâ'an 'alâ hâzâ)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic بِنَاءً (bināʔan), adverbial accusative of بِنَاء (bināʔ). By surface analysis, بنا (benâ) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic بِنَاءً عَلَى هَٰذَا (bināʔan ʕalā hāḏā).
Borrowed from Arabic بني آدم (banī ʔādam, “sons of Adam”)
Borrowed from Arabic بُنْيَان (bunyān), perhaps influenced by بنیاد (bonyâd, “foundation, basis”).
Borrowed from Arabic بَهِيمَة (bahīma), possibly borrowed from Biblical Hebrew בְּהֵמָה (bəhēmā́).
Borrowed from Arabic بَوَاسِير (bawāsīr), plural of بَاسُور (bāsūr, “haemorrhoids”).
Borrowed from Arabic أَبُو ٱلْعَجَب (ʔabū l-ʕajab).
بو (bu, from Arabic أَبُو (ʔabū, used to form nicknames, literally “father of”)) + تیمار (timâr, “worry; sorrow”).

Borrowed from Arabic أَبُوقَلَمُون (ʔabūqalamūn), from Ancient Greek ὑποκάλαμον (hupokálamon), originally a Byzantine term used to refer to a precious multi-coloured textile, later used to refer to the bird due to its ability to change the colours of its feathers .

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic طَاق (ṭāq), borrowed from a Middle Iranian language, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg-.
Borrowed from Arabic [Term?], itself borrowed from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (tʾk' /⁠tāg⁠/, “item; unit; single; branch”). Doublet of تا (tâ), which is inherited.
Borrowed from Arabic طَاقَة (ṭāqa), from طَاقَ (ṭāqa).

parole.significato: horoscope; omen; star of fortune (in astrology)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic طَبَق (ṭabaq), from Middle Persian tʾp̄k' (/⁠tābag⁠/). Doublet of تاوه (tāwa /tâve, “frying pan”).
Borrowed from Arabic طَبْل (ṭabl). Compare Doublet of تبیر (tabir, “drum”).
Borrowed from Arabic طِبِّيّ (ṭibbiyy). By surface analysis, طب (tebb, “medicine”) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic طَرْز (ṭarz), from Persian درز (darz), from Proto-Iranian *darz- (“to fasten, to sew”).

parole.significato: the two parties (relating to a dispute, a case, a treaty, a negotiation, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic طَرَفَيْن (ṭarafayn), dual of طَرَف (ṭaraf). By surface analysis, طرف (taraf, “side”) + ـین (-eyn).
Borrowed from Arabic طُفَيْل (ṭufayl); see there for more.

parole.significato: rise of a celestial body; (especially) sunrise

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic طَمَع (ṭamaʕ). Northern Luri: تمٮا (temaa)
Borrowed from Arabic أَطْنَاب (ʔaṭnāb), plural of طُنُب (ṭunub, “rope”). Majorly displaced native رَسَن (rasan) and اَرویس (arvês) (from Middle Persian [script needed] (’lwys /⁠arwēs⁠/)).
Borrowed from Arabic طُوفَان (ṭūfān). Folk etymology incorrectly derives it from توفیدن (tōfīdan /tufidan).
Borrowed from Arabic طُومَار (ṭūmār), from Byzantine Greek τομάριον (tomárion).
Borrowed from Arabic طَوِيلَة (ṭawīla). Sense 1 is from طُوَالَة (ṭuwāla, “stable”).

parole.significato: during, over, over the course of
the name of the Arabic script letter ظ

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic ظَاهِر (ẓāhir), from ظَهَرَ (ẓahara).
Borrowed from Arabic ظَاهِرًا (ẓāhiran), from ظَاهِر (ẓāhir). By surface analysis, ظاهر (zâher) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic عَازِم (ʕāzim), from عَزَمَ (ʕazama).
Borrowed from Arabic عَالِم (ʕālim), from عَلِمَ (ʕalima).
Borrowed from Arabic عَامَّة (ʕāmma, “most general part of; common people”)

parole.significato: pro bono, for the public good.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عام (ʕām, “public”) + Arabic منفعة (“benefit”).

parole.significato: A long gown or cloak open at the front, worn by clergy in Iran.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عِبْرَانِيّ (ʕibrāniyy), ultimately from Hebrew עִבְרִי ('ivrí, ʿiḇrī).
From Arabic عِبْرِيّ (ʕibriyy), itself derived from Hebrew עִבְרִי (ʿivrī́, “Hebrew”).

parole.significato: classifier for units of an object

parole.testo: From عدس (adas, “lentil”) + ـی (-i). "Lens": semantic loan from Arabic عَدَسَة (ʕadasa).
Borrowed from Arabic عَرَبِيّ (ʕarabiyy), from عَرَب (ʕarab, “Arabs”) + ـِيّ (-iyy).
Ezafe of عرض ('arz) from Arabic عَرْض (ʕarḍ, “presentation”) + حال (hâl) from Arabic حَال (ḥāl, “case, state of things”).

parole.significato: knowledge, knowing, cognition, especially in Sufism

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَرُوس (ʕarūs). Displaced Persian بیو (bayu) to a large extent.
Borrowed from Arabic عِزَّة (ʕizza), from عَزَّ (ʕazza).
Borrowed from Arabic عَزْم (ʕazm), from عَزَمَ (ʕazama).

parole.significato: night watch, nocturnal patrol, nocturnal police
sap, extract (somewhat viscose liquid that one obtains by wringing)
infallibility; protection from sin (e.g. of the Shi'a imams)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عُضْوِيَّة (ʕuḍwiyya). By surface analysis, عضو (ozv, “member”) + ـیت (-iyyat).
Borrowed from Arabic عُقَاب (ʕuqāb). Displaced native آله (âloh).
Borrowed from Arabic عِقَاب (ʕiqāb), from عَاقَبَ (ʕāqaba).
Borrowed from Arabic عَقِيدَة (ʕaqīda), from the root ع ق د (ʕ q d).

parole.significato: aqiqah (the sacrifice of an animal after childbirth)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَلَامَة تَعَجُّب (ʕalāmat taʕajjub), equivalent to عَلامَت ('alâmat, “mark”) + تَعَجُّب (ta'ajjob, “astonishment”).
Borrowed from Arabic عَلَف (ʕalaf). Somewhat eclipsed native اسپست (aspast) and واش (vâš) in standard Persian.
Borrowed from Arabic عِلْم (ʕilm), from عَلِمَ (ʕalima).
Borrowed from Arabic عِلْمِيّ (ʕilmiyy), from عِلْم (ʕilm) or ـِيّ (-iyy). By surface analysis, علم (ilm /elm) + ـی (-ī /-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: of or pertaining to Ali (the first Shia imam)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَلَوِيّ (ʕalawiyy). By surface analysis, علی (“Ali”) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: upon, over, on (only used in borrowed Arabic phrases; see related terms below)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَلَى الرَّغْمِ (ʕalā ar-raḡmi). By surface analysis, علی (alâ) + رغم (raġm) + ی (-e, the ezâfe).
Borrowed from Arabic عَلَيْهِ (ʕalayhi, “upon him”) (pronounced عَلَيْه (ʕalayh) in pausa), third-person singular masculine of عَلَى (ʕalā).
Borrowed from Arabic عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ (ʕalayhi s-salāmu).

parole.significato: blessings and peace be upon him
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَلَيْهِ ٱلصَّلَاةُ وَٱلسَّلَامُ (ʕalayhi ṣ-ṣalātu was-salāmu).
Borrowed from Arabic عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ (ʕalayhā s-salāmu).

parole.significato: umrah (a minor hajj, a lesser pilgrimage to Mecca, other than at the time of the hajj)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَمَلِيَّات (ʕamaliyyāt), plural of Arabic عَمَلِيَّة (ʕamaliyya).
Borrowed from Arabic عُمُومًا (ʕumūman). By surface analysis, عموم (umūm /omum) + ـاً (-an).

parole.significato: synonym of سیمرغ (simorġ, a mythical bird)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَنْكَبُوت (ʕankabūt). Displaced native جولا (jōlā /julâ) in Iranian Persian.

parole.significato: the hoi polloi, the general population
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic عَوَامّ النَّاس (ʕawāmm an-nās).

parole.significato: the pudenda or pudendum, the privy parts; nakedness

parole.testo: Pseudo-Arabism from عَکْس ('aks, “photo”), from Arabic عَكْس (ʕaks, “reflection, opposite”), using the Arabic pattern فَعّال (faʕʕāl) which creates words for habitual actions and professions. Compare کَفّاش (kaffâš, “cobbler”).
Pseudo-Arabism, perhaps coined in Ottoman Turkish عكسالعمل (aksülamel).
Borrowed from Arabic عَيَّاشِي (ʕayyāšī, “related to life or breadmaking”). By surface analysis, عَیَّاش (ayyāš /eyyâš) + ـِی (-ī /-i).
Borrowed from Arabic عَيْش (ʕayš), from عَاشَ (ʕāša).
Borrowed from Arabic عَيْن (ʕayn, “eye; thing itself”).
Borrowed from Arabic عَيْنِيّ (ʕayniyy). By surface analysis, عین (eyn) + ـی (-i).

parole.significato: agrimony (Agrimonia gen. et spp.), especially the common agrimony (Agrimonia eupatoria)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic غَافِل (ḡāfil), active participle of غَفَلَ (ḡafala).
Borrowed from Arabic غَالِبًا (ḡāliban). By surface analysis, غالب (ġâleb) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic غِرْبَال (ḡirbāl), from Aramaic עַרְבָּלָא / ܥܱܪܒܳܠܴܐ (ʿarbālā), assumed to be from Hurrian.

parole.significato: exile (as a state); being away from one's native land

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic غَرْبِيّ (ḡarbiyy). By surface analysis, غرب (ġarb, “west”) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: ghazal (a poetic form mostly used for love poetry in Middle Eastern, South, and Central Asian poetry)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic غَزَل (ḡazal, “a compliment; erotic poetry”).

parole.significato: cereal, corn, grain (type of plant and its fruit)
the unseen; the mysterious and invisible, known only to God and the prophets and imams

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic غَيْر إِنْسَانِيّ (ḡayr ʔinsāniyy). By surface analysis, غیرـ (ġeyr-e-) + انسانی (ensâni).

parole.significato: "protective jealousy", honor, possessiveness; an emotion which drives one to protect one's family members from the othe…

parole.testo: From Arabic غَيْر طَبِيعِيّ (ḡayr ṭabīʕiyy). Morphologically from غیرـ (ġeyr-e-) + طبیعی (tabi'i).
Borrowed from Arabic غَيْر قَانُونِيّ (ḡayr qānūniyy). By surface analysis, غیرـ (ġayr-i-) + قانونی (qānūnī).
Borrowed from Arabic غَيْر مُمْكِن (ḡayr mumkin). By surface analysis, غیرـ (ġeyr-e-) + ممکن (momken).
Borrowed from Arabic غَيْر مَنْقُول (ḡayr manqūl). By surface analysis, غیرـ (ġeyr-e-) + منقول (manqul).

parole.significato: Used to form adverbs from nouns or adjectives.
forms the plural of some nouns; such plurals often have a collective sense, e.g. referring to products or plants
parole.testo: An extended form of ـات (-ât), from Arabic ـَات (-āt). The /dʒ/ goes back to the Middle Persian /ɡ/ that also resurfaces with the plural suffix ـان (-ân), as in پرنده (parande) → پرندگان (parandegân). Before the Arabic suffix, this /ɡ/ was Arabised to /dʒ/ by analogy with Persian loanwords in Arabic

parole.significato: a condition or state of being the thing or being in the role denoted by the noun it is suffixed to; -ness
a plural suffix used with certain nouns denoting persons, generally of Arabic origin
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic ـِينَ (-īna, genitive/accusative plural suffix). The case distinction, which is alien to Modern Persian, was lost, but the Arabic nominative form ـُونَ (-ūna) came to be used with nisba nouns for euphonic reasons.
Borrowed from Arabic فَائِدَة (fāʔida), from فَادَ (fāda).

parole.significato: fatwa (legal opinion, decree or ruling issued by a mufti)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فَخْر (faḵr, “honour, pride”), the Arabic word itself could be an Iranian borrowing ultimately from Proto-Iranian *huHarnā́h (“splendour, glory”). Doublet of فَرّ (farr). See the Arabic root ف خ ر (f ḵ r) and Proto-Iranian *huHarnā́h (“splendour, glory”) for more detailed etymol

parole.significato: one who willingly risks or sacrifices his or her life for another person

parole.testo: Reborrowed from Arabic فِرْدَوْس (firdaws), ultimately from Proto-Iranian *paridayjah, like the native پالیز (pālēz /pâliz).

parole.significato: the Persians, the Iranians (as a whole); Iran, Persia

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فِرْعَوْن (firʕawn), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܦܹܪܥܘܼܢ, borrowed from Koine Greek Φαραών (Pharaṓn), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew פַּרְעֹה, borrowed from Egyptian pr-ꜥꜣ, from pr + ꜥꜣ.
Borrowed from Arabic فَرْعِيّ (farʕiyy). By surface analysis, فرع (far') + ـی (-i).
Borrowed from Arabic فَصْل (faṣl). Displaced native هنگام (hangâm, “season”) and فرگرد (fargard, “chapter”).

parole.significato: nature, the innate characteristics of a thing.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فِعْل مُتَعَدٍّ (fiʕl mutaʕaddin).

parole.significato: now, for now, for the time being, presently

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فِعْلِيّ (fiʕliyy). By surface analysis, فعل (fe'l) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: case, instance, item, entry; also used as a counter.
fiqh (jurisprudence in the Islamic law, shari'a)
jurist and theologian, expert in Islamic jurisprudence.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فَلَاة (falāh). In the modern sense, a phono-semantic matching of French plateau or another European language, compare English flat.
Borrowed from Arabic فَلَافِل (falāfil), broken plural of فِلْفِل (filfil); see فلفل (filfil /felfel) for more.

parole.significato: so-and-so, such-and-such; a generic placeholder name, used when one does not wish to specify a name.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فِلِزّ (filizz), from Classical Syriac ܦܠܙܐ (plezzā), from Parthian 𐫛𐫓𐫏𐫗𐫝 (plync /⁠plinǰ⁠/). Doublet of برنج (berenj, “brass; bronze”) and برنز (boronz, “bronze”).
Borrowed from Arabic فَلْس (fals), from Ancient Greek φολίς (pholís).

parole.significato: pepper (including sweet peppers, chilis as well as black pepper)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فِلْفِل (filfil), from Classical Persian پلپل (pilpil), from Sanskrit पिप्पलि (pippali, “long pepper”), ultimately from Dravidian. Compare Tamil திப்பலி (tippali), Swahili pilipili, Aramaic פלפלא (pelplā), Hebrew פלפל (pilpél), Old Armenian պղպեղ (płpeł), պղպիղ (płpił), Armenian

parole.significato: sky, the sphere of the heavens, the firmament

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic فَنّ (fann), from Persian پند (pand, “knack, trick”).

Borrowed from Arabic فِنْجَان (finjān), borrowed from Classical Persian پِنْگَان (pingān), possibly borrowed from Classical Syriac ܦܝܢܟܐ (pīnəḵā), from Aramaic פִּינְכָא (pīnəkā), borrowed from Ancient Greek πίναξ (pínax).
Borrowed from Arabic فُنْدُق (funduq), borrowed from Middle Persian pndk' (pondik), borrowed from Ancient Greek Ποντικὸν κάρυον (Pontikòn káruon), from Ποντῐκόν (Pontĭkón) + κᾰ́ρῠον (kắrŭon).

Borrowed from Arabic فُنْدُق (funduq), borrowed from Ancient Greek πανδοκεῖον (pandokeîon), from πᾰν- (păn-, “all, every”) + δοκ- (dok-, o-grade of the stem of δέχομαι (dékhomai, “to receive”)) + -εῖον (-eîon).

parole.significato: to understand (hear correctly and know the language)
parole.testo: فهم (fahm) + ـیدن (-idan), from Arabic فَهْم (fahm). Compare Central Kurdish فامین (famîn), فام کردن (fam kirdin), Northern Kurdish fehm kirin, Southern Kurdish فەهمین (fehmîn), Zazaki fam kerden, Northern Luri فںمسێ (fəmesı).
Borrowed from Arabic فَوْج (fawj), from فَيْج (fayj), borrowed from Middle Persian pdk'. Doublet of پیک (peyk).
Pseudo-Arabism. By surface analysis, فوق (fowq) + ذکر (zekr).
Borrowed from Arabic فَوْقَ الْعادة (fawqa al-ʕāda, literally “above the usual”).

Borrowed from Arabic فَيْض (fayḍ, “flood, overflow, abundance”). From the use for the abundance of God’s powers, treasures and gifts, the word develops the sense “grace” (already in Arabic, but less widely used than in Persian).
Borrowed from Arabic فِيل (fīl), borrowed from Middle Persian pyl (/⁠pīl⁠/), from Akkadian 𒄠𒋛 (pīru). Doublet of پیل (pil).
Borrowed from Arabic فَيْلَسُوف (faylasūf), from Ancient Greek φιλόσοφος (philósophos). The Iranian pronunciation was likely influenced by French philosophe.
Unadapted borrowing from Arabic فِيمَا بَيْنَ (fīmā bayna).
Unadapted borrowing from Arabic فِي ٱلْبَدَاهَةِ (fī l-badāhati).

parole.significato: coming short; failing (to do); helpless, weak

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic قَالِب (qālib). Doublet of کالبد (kâlbod).
Borrowed from Arabic قَامُوس (qāmūs), from Ancient Greek ὠκεανός (ōkeanós). Doublet of اقیانوس (uqyānūs /oġyânus).

Reborrowed from Arabic قَبَاء (qabāʔ), from Middle Persian [script needed] (kpʾh /⁠kabāh⁠/, “garment, cloak”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kep- (“to split, cut”). Cognate to Central Kurdish کەوا (kewa, “long garment open in front”) and Khotanese [script needed] (khapa, “dress”). Perhaps
Borrowed from Arabic قَبْر (qabr). Compare Northern Luri غۏر (qwr).
Borrowed from Arabic قِبْطِيّ (qibṭiyy), from قِبْط (qibṭ, “Copts”) + ـِيّ (-iyy).
Borrowed from Arabic قَبْلًا (qablan). By surface analysis, قبل (qabl /ġabl, “before”) + ـاً (-an, adverbial suffix).
Borrowed from Arabic قُبَّة (qubba). Doublet of گنبد (gunbad /gonbad).
Borrowed from Arabic قَبُول (qabūl, “acceptance, assent, consent”).
Borrowed from Arabic قُدْسِيّ (qudsiyy). By surface analysis, قدس (qods) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: madwort (Alyssum gen. et spp.; even Acanthophyllum bracteatum alias Alyssum bracteatum, and Lobularia maritima alias Al…
parole.testo: Perhaps formed by physicians from the Arabic root ق د م (q d m) related to “advancing, pressing forward” – both possible patterns – as medical practitioners employed the seed mucilage of Alyssum homolocarpum to expectorate and purge kidney stones.

parole.significato: twerk, twerking; gyrating one's hips (used for both men and women)
parole.testo: Francis Joseph Steingass speculates that it is from Arabic قِرْد (qird, “monkey, ape”). His nineteenth-century dictionary gives "monkey" as the only noun definition while marking قر دادن (qer dâdan) as a "modern colloquial" verb for "to coquette about, sway the body as in a dance", so perhaps the ve
Borrowed from Arabic قُرْآنِيّ (qurʔāniyy). By surface analysis, قرآن (qor'ân) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: reading (way to read or understand a text)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic قُرْبَان (qurbān), borrowed from Aramaic קורבנא (qurbānā).

parole.significato: kermes insect (Kermes ilicis, an insect found on the kermes oak that is used to make crimson dyes)
parole.testo: PIE word  *kwŕ̥mis Borrowed from Arabic قِرْمِز (qirmiz), from Persian *کرمست (*kermest), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kŕ̥miš (“worm”), whence also the inherited doublet کرم (kerm, “worm”).
Borrowed from Arabic قِرْمِزِيّ (qirmiziyy). By surface analysis, قرمز (qermez) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic قَرِيب الْوُقُوع (qarīb al-wuqūʕ).
Borrowed from Arabic قِسْمًا (qisman), adverbial accusative of Arabic قِسْم (qism, “part”). By surface analysis, قسم (qism /ġesm, “part”) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic قِسْمَة (qisma), from قَسَمَ (qasama). Cognate with Ottoman Turkish قِسْمَت (kısmet).

parole.significato: synonym of خرمای زاهدی (xormâ-ye zâhedi, “Zahidi palm date”).

parole.testo: Pseudo-Arabism, from the root ق ض ي.
Borrowed from Arabic قَطْرَان (qaṭrān). Also Persian کتران (katrân, “tar; (cedar) resin, pitch”).
Borrowed from Arabic قُقْنُوس (quqnūs), from Ancient Greek κύκνος (kúknos, “swan”).
Borrowed from Arabic قَلْبِيّ (qalbiyy). Equivalent to قلب (qalb) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic اَلْقُلْزُم (al-qulzum), from Ancient Greek Κλύσμα (Klúsma). "Red Sea" > "ocean" (in general).
Borrowed from Arabic قَلَم (qalam), from Ancient Greek κάλαμος (kálamos, “reed”).
Borrowed from Arabic قُلَّة (qulla, “peak, summit, top”).

Borrowed from Arabic غَلْيُون (ḡalyūn, “smoking pipe”), then hypercorrecting the ending [un] which colloquial Iranian Persian generally puts for trailing /ɒn/, with regard to the vulgar origin of the habit of tobacco smoking, which wrong deduction was also supported by reminiscence of Arabic غَلَيَا
Borrowed from Arabic قَمَرِيّ (qamariyy). By surface analysis, قمر (qamar) + ـی (-ī /-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Pseudo-Arabism as an Arabic occupational noun from قند (qand).
Borrowed from Arabic قَنْد (qand), displacing older کند (kand) or کاند (kând).
Borrowed from Arabic قِنْدِيل (qindīl), see there for further information.
Borrowed from Arabic قِنْطَار (qinṭār), from Byzantine Greek κεντηνάριον (kentēnárion), from Latin centēnārium (“hundredweight”).
Borrowed from Arabic قَهْر (qahr, “wrath, frustration”)., Northern Luri غٸر (qəər).

Persian قوسوقزح Reinterpretation of earlier قوسقزح (qaws-i-qazah /ġows-e-ġazah) as a compound, from Arabic قَوْس قُزَح (qaws quzaḥ, literally “bow of the pre-Islamic Arab god Quzah”). By surface analysis, قوس (qaws /ġows, “bow”) + قزح (qazah /ġazah, “Quzah”)
Borrowed from Arabic قَوْمِيَّة (qawmiyya), or by surface analysis, قوم (qawm/ġowm, “nation”) + ـیت (-iyat).

parole.significato: maulana; a title for religious scholars, most famously held by the poet Rumi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic مَوْلَانَا (mawlānā), from مَوْلًى (mawlan, “lord”) + possessive suffix ـنَا (-nā).
Borrowed from Arabic مَوْلُود (mawlūd). The sense "birthday, nativity" came from a confusion with Arabic مَوْلِد (mawlid).

parole.significato: client (of a lawyer, agent, or barrister)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic مَيْدَان (maydān), itself an Iranian borrowing. Doublet of میان (miyān /miyân).
Borrowed from Arabic مَيْمُون (maymūn), from يَمَنَ (yamana).
Borrowed from Arabic مِينَا (mīnā). Doublet of مینو (minu).

parole.significato: Seville orange, bitter orange, Citrus aurantium
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic نَارَنْج (nāranj), from Classical Persian نارنگ (nārang).

parole.significato: namus: notion of honor, moral reputation, and female chastity
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic نَامُوس (nāmūs), from Ancient Greek νόμος (nómos).

The adjective is most probably from ناـ (nâ-, “non-, un-”) + آهار (âhâr, “food, stew”), exactly equivalent to Sanskrit अनाहार (anāhāra, “not taking food, abstinent”). Compare with Sogdian 𐼻𐼰𐼳𐼰𐽀 (nʾhʾr /⁠nāhār⁠/, “un-food (lit.), hungry”) and also Old Armenian նիհար (nihar, “skinny”), an Iranian borr
Borrowed from Arabic نَبَاتِيّ (nabātiyy). By surface analysis, نبات (nabât) + ـی (-i).
Borrowed from Arabic نَبِيّ (nabiyy), from Aramaic נְבִיָּא (nəḇiyyā) (absolutive form: נְבִי (nəḇī)). Compare Hebrew נָבִיא (nāḇīʔ).
Borrowed from Arabic نَجَاة (najāh, “survival, salvation”), verbal form of نَجَا (najā, “to escape”).
Borrowed from Arabic نُجُوم (nujūm). Originally short for علم نجوم (elm-e nojum, “science of the stars”).
نُجوم (nojum) + ـی (-i), or directly from Arabic نُجُومِيّ (nujūmiyy). For the sense "very large," presumably a semantic loan from French astronomique or a semantic loan from English astronomical.

parole.significato: dispute, quarrel, fight; (especially) street fight, brawl

parole.testo: Pseudo-Arabism from نازک (nāzuk) using the Arabic pattern فَعالة (faʕāla), which often forms abstract nouns.
Borrowed from Arabic نِسْبَةً (nisbatan). By surface analysis, نِسْبَت (nisbat) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic نِظَامِيّ (niẓāmiyy). By surface analysis, نظام (nizām /nezâm) + ـی (-ī /-i, suffix forming adjectives).

parole.significato: Nizamiyya (any one of educational institutions founded in the 11th century by Nizam al-Mulk, vizier of the Saljuq Empir…
parole.testo: From Arabic نِظَامِيَّة (niẓāmiyya). By surface analysis, نظام (nizām /nezâm) + ـیه (-iyya /-iye).
Borrowed from Arabic نَظَرِيَّة (naẓariyya). By surface analysis, نظر (nazar) + ـیه (-iyya /-iye).
Borrowed from Arabic نَعْش (naʕš). If that is of Iranian origin, doublet of لاش (lâš).
Borrowed from Arabic نَوْبَة (nawba). Displaced native پستا (pastā).
Analyzable as نور (nur) + ـانی (-âni); compare خوبانی (xubâni). Possibly borrowed from, modeled after, or influenced by Arabic نُورَانِيّ (nūrāniyy).
Borrowed from Arabic نَيْسَان (naysān), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܢܝܣܢ (nīsān), from Aramaic נִיסָן (nīsān), borrowed from Akkadian 𒌚𒁈 (nisannum).
Borrowed from Arabic هالة (hāla, “halo”), from Ancient Greek ἅλως (hálōs, “halo”).

parole.significato: a separation or remoteness from one's friend, beloved, or homeland

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic هَرْج وَمَرْج (harj wamarj).
Borrowed from Arabic هَرَوِيّ (harawiyy), from هَرَاة (harāh, “Herat”) + ـِيّ (-iyy). Compare Persian حموی (hamavi), from Arabic حَمَوِيّ (ḥamawiyy), from حَمَاة (ḥamāh, “Hamat”) + ـِيّ (-iyy).
Borrowed from Arabic هَلَاك (halāk), from هَلَكَ (halaka), from Proto-Semitic *halak-.

parole.significato: hamza (Arabic sign representing the glottal stop)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic هَنْدَسَة (handasa), itself a Middle Persian borrowing.
Probably from Arabic هِنْدِيّ (hindiyy). By surface analysis, هند (hind /hend, “India”) + ـی (-ī /-i, suffix forming adjectives). Compare native هندو (hindū /hendu).
Borrowed from Arabic هَوَائِيّ (hawāʔiyy). By surface analysis, هوا (havâ) + ـی (-i, nisba suffix).

Borrowed from Arabic حُبَارَى (ḥubārā), the original Arabic name for Chlamydotis macqueenii, also applied for the temperate climate Otis tarda and other fowls of the family when the Arabs faced North. Reinterpreted in Persian as آهو (âhu, “gazelle”) + بره (barre, “lamb”) because it runs as fast as t

parole.significato: violent desire; lust; passion; shallow love

parole.testo: Corrupted from Arabic حَوَائِج القِدْر (ḥawāʔij al-qidr, “kitchen provisions”, literally “the necessaries of the cooking pot”).

parole.significato: Name of the thirty-first letter of the Persian alphabet ه.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic هاء (hāʔ) with vowel shift due to imala
Borrowed from Arabic هَيُولَى (hayūlā), from Ancient Greek ῡ̔́λη (hū́lē). "Primitive formless base of matter" > "monster, bizarre and supernatural creature".
Probably a spelling pronunciation of Arabic وَغَيْرُهُ (waḡayruhu, literally “and other than it”).
Borrowed from Arabic وَارِدَات (wāridāt, “imported goods”), plural of وَارِد (wārid) or Persian plural of وارده (vârede).

parole.significato: middleman, intermediary, mediator (in commerce, conflicts, etc.)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic واقِعاً (wāqiʕan) By surface analysis, واقع (wāqi' /vâġe') + ـا (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic وَاقِعِيّ (wāqiʕiyy). By surface analysis, واقع (wāqi' /vâġe') + ـی (-ī /i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic وَاقِعِيَّة (wāqiʕiyya). By surface analysis, واقع (wāqi' /vâġe') + ـیت (-iyyat /iyat).
Borrowed from Arabic وَإِلَّا (wa-ʾillā). By surface analysis, و (va) + الا (ellâ).
Borrowed from Arabic وَالِد (wālid), from وَلَدَ (walada), from Proto-Semitic *walad-.
Borrowed from Arabic وَالِدَة (wālida). By surface analysis, والد (wālid /vâled) + ـه (-a /-e).
Borrowed from Arabic وَالِدَيْن (wālidayn), oblique dual of وَالِد (wālid). By surface analysis, والد (wālid /vâled) + ـین (-ayn /-eyn).

parole.significato: that's that, end of story, period
parole.testo: From the Arabic phrase وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ (wa-s-salāmu ʕalaykum wa-raḥmatu llāhi wa-barakātuhu, “May the peace, mercy, and blessing of God be upon you!”), a phrase used at the end of speeches, especially Islamic ones.
Borrowed from Arabic وَٱللّٰهِ (wal-lāhi, “by God”). By surface analysis, و (wa /va, “and”) + الله (allāh /allâh, “God”).

parole.significato: a governor of a large province

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic وَا وَيْلَا (wā waylā). Equivalent to وا (vâ) + ویل (veyl).

parole.significato: sum of money, amount of money

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic وَحْشِيّ (waḥšiyy). Equivalent to وحش (vahš) + ـی (-i).
Borrowed from Arabic وَرْد (ward), itself of Iranian origin and from the same etymon as native گل (gol).
Derived from Arabic وَزِير أَعْظَم (wazīr ʔaʕẓam).
Borrowed from Arabic وَضْعِيَّة (waḍʕiyya). By surface analysis, وضع (waz' /vaz') + ـیت (-iyyat /-iyat).

parole.significato: wudu (a ritual washing of the forearms, head, and feet, required after minor impurity, frequently performed immediately…

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic وَقْت (waqt), itself of uncertain origin, see the Arabic entry for more.

parole.significato: “Guardianship of the Islamic Jurists”; a system of government wherein the Islamic clergy (ulema) have the ultimate say…
parole.testo: Calque of Arabic وِلَايَة الْفَقِيه (wilāyat al-faqīh).
From earlier ولیکن (walēkin), from Arabic وَلٰكِن (walākin) or a conjugation of و (wa) and لیکن (lēkin) from Arabic لٰكِن (lākin).
Borrowed from Arabic وَلِيّ (waliyy), from the root و ل ي (w l y).
Borrowed from Arabic وَلِيّ عَهْد (waliyy ʕahd). By surface analysis, ولی (vali) + عهد (ahd).
Borrowed from Arabic كاشِف (kāšif), from كَشَفَ (kašafa).

parole.significato: Name of (ک), the Persian form of the letter kaf, representing the sound /k/.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic كَانُون الْأَوَّل (kānūn al-ʔawwal).
Borrowed from Arabic كَانُون الثَّانِي (kānūn aṯ-ṯānī).
Borrowed from Arabic كَاكَنْج (kākanj), from Middle Persian [script needed] (kākanag). Doublet of کاکنه (kâkone), which was inherited.
Borrowed from Arabic كِبْرِيت (kibrīt, “sulfur, match”), from Aramaic כִּבְּרִיתָא (kiḇrīṯā) / ܟܶܒܪܺܝܬܳܐ (kĕḇrīṯā, “sulfur”), from Akkadian 𒆠𒀀𒀭𒀀𒇉 (kibrītu, “sulfur; firebrand”).

parole.significato: great (title referring to an important leader)
flax (the plant or fibers of Linum usitatissimum)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic كُتُبِيّ (kutubiyy). By surface analysis, کتب (kutub /kotob) + ـی (-ī /-i, nominal suffix)
Pseudo-Arabism formed from the Arabic root ك ت ب (k t b).
Ultimately from Arabic [Term?], related to كَتَبَ (kataba, “to write”).

Borrowed from Arabic كَثَافَة (kaṯāfa, “density”). The semantic shift from Arabic is explained by the fact that in some Arabic and Persian dialects dirt (soil) is used in the sense of bulk density, as the latter property denotes the magnitude of solids like mineral components such as soil/earth/dirt

parole.significato: rent, fee for using another's property:

parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy), borrowed from Aramaic כּוּרְסְיָא (kursəyā) or Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܣܝܐ (kursəyā).

Borrowed from Arabic كِرْيَاس (kiryās). In Arabic, this is a rooftop privy whose contents fall outside the house; however, in Persian, the meaning was changed early on to refer to the place where the contents would fall, i.e. immediately outside the gate.
Borrowed from Arabic كَسَاد (kasād), but the adjectival meaning is properly from كَاسِد (kāsid).
Pseudo-Arabism from کفش (kafš, “shoe”), using the Arabic pattern فَعّال (faʕʕāl), which creates words for habitual actions and professions. Compare عکاس ('akkâs, “photographer”).
Borrowed from Arabic كُلّ (kull), from Proto-Semitic *kull-, from Proto-Afroasiatic *ʔa-kʷall-.
Borrowed from Arabic كَلْب (kalb), from Proto-Semitic *kalb-.
Borrowed from Arabic كِلْس (kils), borrowed from Classical Syriac ܟܠܫܐ (kelšā), borrowed from Ancient Greek χάλιξ (khálix), possibly borrowed from Pre-Greek.
From Arabic phrase كَمَا كَانَ (kamā kāna, “as it was before”).

parole.significato: the two kinds of existence: the material world and the spiritual world
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic كَوْنَيْن (kawnayn), dual of كَوْن (kawn).
Borrowed from Arabic كَيْفِيَّة (kayfiyya). By surface analysis, کیف (keyf) + ـیت (-iyyat).
Borrowed from Arabic كِيمِيَاء (kīmiyāʔ), from Ancient Greek χῠμείᾱ (khŭmeíā).

parole.significato: o Lord; a supplication to God for aid.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic يَا رَبِّ (yā rabbi).

parole.significato: O Ali; a request for intercession from Ali ibn Abi Talib, the first divinely appointed imam in Shi'ism, the sect follow…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic يَا عَلِيُّ (yā ʕaliyyu).
Borrowed from Arabic يَافَا (yāfā), borrowed from Biblical Hebrew יָפוֹ (yāfō).
Borrowed from Arabic يَاقُوت (yāqūt), from Ancient Greek ὑάκινθος (huákinthos). Doublet of یاکند (yâkand).
Unadapted borrowing from Arabic يَحْتَمِلُ (yaḥtamilu), conjugated form of اِحْتَمَلَ (iḥtamala).

parole.significato: indeed, definitely, for sure, surely, undoubtedly
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic يَقِينًا (yaqīnan), adverbial accusative of يَقِين (yaqīn). By surface analysis, یقین (yaqin) + ـاً (-an).
Borrowed from Arabic يَهُودِيّ (yahūdiyy). By surface analysis, یهود (yahud) + ـی (-i, suffix forming adjectives).
Borrowed from Arabic يَهُودِيَّة (yahūdiyya). By surface analysis, یهود (yahūd /yahud) + ـیت (-iyyat /-iyat).
From Arabic عَلَف (ʕalaf), possibly via a Turkic source.
